summary: A new atomic layer deposition (ALD) process was applied for the homogeneous coating of carbon nanotubes with vanadium oxide. The process allows the coating of the inner and outer surfaces with a highly conformal film of controllable thickness, enabling the production of high surface area hybrid materials. The ALD-coated tubes are used as active components in gas-sensing devices, showing electric responses directly related to the p-n heterojunction formed between the support and the film.
evidence: A new atomic layer deposition (ALD) process was applied for the homogeneous coating of carbon nanotubes with vanadium oxide. It permits the coating of the inner and outer surface with a highly conformal film of controllable thickness and, hence, the production of high surface area hybrid materials at a so far unprecedented quality. The ALD-coated tubes are used as active component in gas-sensing devices. They show electric responses that are directly related to the peculiar structure, i.e., the p -n heterojunction formed between the support and the film.
